verdict.rationale: First-party docs describe Whistle, a 16.9 MB on-CPU speech-to-text model covering seven languages, and `needle.stream(chunks)`, which transcribes live from the microphone and commits words once two passes agree. Word timestamps and keyword biasing are also documented, and the site states no data leaves the device. The engine additionally exposes speech APIs. Missing for 10: independent hands-on corroboration of Whistle's real-time streaming (the one community mic-transcription mention concerns Cactus Hybrid/Gemma, not Whistle), and any documented latency or accuracy figures for live dictation.
